The central tree is reduced from 157 to 95 lines (39.5%) and from 10,777 to 6,665 characters (38.2%). It emphasizes boundaries, shared dependencies and transport transitions. Six peripherals hold configuration mechanics, dependency rules, concrete connections, evaluation callbacks, HTTP decisions and cleanup order. M = modular structure; C = calls; O = ownership/lifetime; D = data dependencies across those views.

The runtime critique is addressed by removing the central constructor inventory, giving detailed mechanisms a peripheral home, and aligning peripheral positions with their attachment rows. Evaluation now sits beside its evaluation anchor. Text rectangles do not overlap; all edge endpoints are valid and all diagrams are connected.

Evidence comes only from the supplied point definition and pinned source texts. bootstrap.ts establishes construction and sharing; vitePlugin.ts establishes transport and shutdown; the two routes.ts files establish dispatch; vite.config.ts establishes configuration; dependencies.test.ts establishes static constraints. In particular, bootstrap constructs one CanvasApiProjection and supplies it to both LiveCanvasService and AgentDiagrammingSessionService: sharing is established within this backend instance.

Seed refinements: the HTTP gate checks a falsy binding header, not merely header absence, and applies only to classified agent mutations. Shutdown registration requires an httpServer. Additional source-backed details include test exclusions, source-root defaults, named evaluation collections, definitions checking capability before reading the body, and DELETE /diagrams/publish falling through to diagrams.delete('publish') if admitted by the adapter. That last statement establishes dispatch, not deletion success. Cleanup has no local exception isolation; a synchronous disposer throw preventing later calls is an inference from the shown sequence.

Related-point labels use only relationship IDs supplied in context.json. The critique's suggestions to import context-status or receipt behavior from other canvases are not adopted: those implementations are outside the pinned evidence. Other points are neither recreated nor treated as sources. Imported mutation classification, handler internals, source classification and disposer implementations remain unverified. The binding-header exception establishes no authentication guarantee, and these call paths do not establish observed execution. Connector rendering remains unverified.

The central tree reduces the seed from 106 to 69 lines (34.9%) and from 8,407 to 5,104 characters excluding the seed's trailing newline (39.3%). It organizes the runtime around boundaries, ownership, transitions and handoffs. Five peripherals provide mechanisms and exceptions. Session lifecycle and dirty-state formulas now have one primary explanatory location. Data dependency remains a cross-cutting computation view rather than another organizational hierarchy.

Source-grounded corrections: MappingEditorRuntime.ts:144-147 deletes the entire detected clone batch when any clone is unsupported, rather than removing only unsupported clones. MappingPage.tsx:468-470 registers all non-hidden drafts, including inactive ones. Explicit save captures state, calls sync([id]), flushes, checks the captured version, then publishes; sync is not passed the captured document (912-927). Generic apply has no explicit flush in its branch, unlike create-diagrams and canvas-generation (316-330, 434-458). Projection-copy navigation replaces only the child session and preserves the source archive (788-808), qualifying the seed's general transfer description.

Details absent from the seed include copy isolation and selective store publication (canvasWorkspace.ts:42-90; canvasSession.ts:69-84), fixed sizing after native resize (MappingEditorRuntime.ts:175-192), projection exclusions and focus invalidation (shapeProjection.ts:26-43; CanvasRuntimeContext.tsx:123-179), and deferred worker-failure publication (NativeRoutingStore.ts:86-115).

The critique's repetition, attachment-scope and placement recommendations are applied. Related-point labels use only relationships supplied in context.json. Cross-point reconciliation is not adopted where it would require unprovided evidence; other points are not recreated. Controller, persistence adapter, bridge, receiver and worker implementations remain outside the pinned sources, so visible calls do not establish their internal guarantees. Previous output and critique were used as review material, not code evidence.

All trees contain printable ASCII and LF newlines. Validated 1-based concept endpoints, connectivity, character limits and nonoverlapping text rectangles. Peripherals sit near their attachment rows with clear column gaps. Rendered connector routing and interaction behavior remain unverified.

canvas.explanation:
The central tree is reduced from 116 to 70 lines (39.7%) and from 8,478 to 5,234 characters (38.3%). It retains responsibilities and main handoffs. Five peripherals contain detailed validation, retry decisions, record publication, evidence transport, and diagram identity checks. M = modular structure, C = call flow, O = ownership, D = data dependency.

The critique is addressed by relocating numeric limits, locking sequences and validation exceptions, attaching expansions at meaningful concepts, and placing peripherals near their central anchors. Comment retries have a separate metadata anchor from create/fork retries. Textual pointers to source, storage and diagrams use the relationships supplied in context.json; no other point is recreated. The JSON passed schema validation. All diagrams are connected, edge endpoints were checked, and measured text rectangles do not overlap. Rendered connector routing remains unverified.

Grounding: agentContext.ts supplies validation/conversion; agentContextLibrary.ts and savedAgentContext.ts supply reuse and metadata contracts; fileAgentContextRepository.ts supplies receipts and publication; fileAgentContextSources.ts supplies capture/transport; diagramAgentContext.ts supplies compilation and backing checks. Details absent from the seed include missing-attachment acceptance, repeated-reference byte accounting, insertion-order cache eviction, sourceId fallback, optional inline descriptor hashes, and full-record reads behind summaries.

Corrections: missing-link/cycle checks cover only the traversed trajectory slice, while entry-ID uniqueness covers all supplied entries. Identical comment retries return before checking the current snapshot hash, correcting the seed's blanket stale-hash failure claim. Diagram loading verifies backing identity without comparing current evidence or revision; background text requests current diagram input, but these files do not establish that later requests supply it. The source adapter enforces 16 MiB despite stale 2 MiB wording. HEAD reuse compares file-representation hashes after LF/CRLF splitting, so the seed's exact-byte wording is narrowed. Portable conversion recomputes the descriptor hash without guaranteeing a different value.

The critique's proposed reconciliation with agent-API status behavior cannot be verified from the pinned inputs. That behavior and external diagram IDs are therefore not imported as evidence; the freshness limitation is explicitly local to the supplied functions. Imported source-range helpers, ImmutableRecords internals, and session-launch callers remain outside the supplied evidence. Previous output and critique served only as review material and were not modified.

The central tree is reduced from 113 lines/8,960 characters to 69 lines/5,881 characters: 38.9% fewer lines and 34.4% fewer characters. Six peripherals give mechanisms a primary explanatory location: push resolution, workflow lifetime, capture provenance, change derivation/replay, review recovery, and record publication. M = modular structure, C = calls, O = ownership, D = data dependency. Nesting groups concepts; only explicit call sequences imply order.

Following the critique, the center emphasizes owners, inputs, transitions, and handoffs. Numeric limits, queue mechanics, classification rules, and recovery details live in peripherals. Peripherals sit beside their attachment regions. All seven trees are connected; edge endpoints and nonoverlapping text bounds were checked. Rendered connector routing remains unverified.

Evidence comes only from the point definition and six pinned source texts. Push details use pushIntegrationService.ts and gitPushSource.ts; workflow details use diffSessionWorkflowService.ts; capture, edits, and acceptance use changeSessionService.ts; record details use changeSessionRecords.ts and diagramChangeSession.ts. Source additions beyond the seed include endpoint comparison with empty commit lists, separate API receipt queues, four-preview batches, manifest-token contents, and hunk-context validation.

Corrections to the seed: existing push deliveries can replay before enablement checks; capture skips unrelated repository documents before snapshots and rejects a mismatch detected afterward; final proposal validation occurs after runAgentWorkflow returns, outside the agent-step callback; history/tree/migration edits can finish ready when the same update explicitly requests and passes readiness validation. The added-diagram rule requires the containing source diagram to exist in the baseline; its owner node may be new.

Point-level handoff references use the supplied relationships: canvas, agent-api, generation, and storage. I did not adopt the critique's suggestion to resolve local uncertainties using other canvases: those sources are outside the permitted evidence. No foreign diagram IDs or implementation guarantees are inferred. The workflow definition, DiffSessionTools internals, repository adapter, catalog publication, and immutable-record helpers are not pinned. Consequently, the diagrams establish observed calls and receipt recovery, not catalog atomicity or the imported workflow's exact scheduling.
